sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q1:whole.hint: Move each wave to the same instant, then combine the displacements at each position.
notes: Superposition adds signed displacements, not speeds or frequencies. Opposite displacements can cancel while the waves continue to travel.
For pulses, first shift each shape by vt in its own travel direction, then add their heights point by point. After overlap, the original pulses continue unchanged in a linear medium.

sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q2:whole.hint: Identify the boundary condition: must the end stay fixed, or can it move?
notes: A pulse reflecting from a fixed end is inverted; reflection from a free end is not. At a junction, distinguish reflected and transmitted pulses.
For reflection of light, incidence and reflection angles are measured from the normal. A plane-mirror image has the same perpendicular distance behind the mirror as the object has in front.

sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q3:whole.hint: Compare wave speeds on the two sides and draw a normal at the boundary.
notes: A wave entering a slower medium bends towards the normal; entering a faster medium bends away. Frequency stays fixed, so wavelength changes in proportion to speed.
Wavefronts are perpendicular to rays. For parallel faces returning to the original medium, the emerging ray is parallel to the incident ray but can be displaced sideways.

sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q4:whole.hint: Compare the wavelength with the opening or obstacle size.
notes: Diffraction becomes more pronounced when the wavelength is comparable with the aperture size. For a single slit, minima satisfy a sin θ = nλ for nonzero integer n.
The central maximum extends to the first minimum on both sides. Its full angular width is approximately 2λ/a at small angles, not λ/a.

sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q5:whole.hint: Compare wave speeds on the two sides and draw a normal at the boundary.
notes: A wave entering a slower medium bends towards the normal; entering a faster medium bends away. Frequency stays fixed, so wavelength changes in proportion to speed.
Wavefronts are perpendicular to rays. For parallel faces returning to the original medium, the emerging ray is parallel to the incident ray but can be displaced sideways.

sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q6:whole.hint: Check whether the question compares amplitude, intensity, or total power; these do not scale in the same way.
notes: For the same medium and frequency, intensity is proportional to amplitude squared. For an isotropic point source, I = P/(4πr²).
When coherent waves overlap, add their signed displacements first and then square the resultant amplitude. Adding intensities alone loses the interference effect.

sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q7:whole.hint: Express the separation as a fraction of a complete wavelength or period.
notes: For a progressive sinusoidal wave, Δφ = 2πΔx/λ, or 2πΔt/T. A complete cycle is 2π radians, not π.
Account for any initial phase difference between the sources as well as the path difference. Equivalent phases differ by whole multiples of 2π.

sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q8:whole.hint: Compare the two path lengths to the observation point. Does their difference reinforce or oppose the waves?
notes: For initially in-phase sources, constructive interference has path difference nλ; destructive interference has (n + ½)λ.
For a double slit at small angles, fringe spacing is λD/d. Use slit separation d, not slit width, and distinguish adjacent-fringe spacing from distance to a particular order.

sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q9:whole.hint: Compare the two path lengths to the observation point. Does their difference reinforce or oppose the waves?
notes: For initially in-phase sources, constructive interference has path difference nλ; destructive interference has (n + ½)λ.
For a double slit at small angles, fringe spacing is λD/d. Use slit separation d, not slit width, and distinguish adjacent-fringe spacing from distance to a particular order.

sup-2612c6d36adf20d7-q10:whole.hint: Check whether the question compares amplitude, intensity, or total power; these do not scale in the same way.
notes: For the same medium and frequency, intensity is proportional to amplitude squared. For an isotropic point source, I = P/(4πr²).
When coherent waves overlap, add their signed displacements first and then square the resultant amplitude. Adding intensities alone loses the interference effect.
